---
title: "metest"
subtitle: "Tests and contrasts of marginal effects"
---
<<dd_version: 2>>

`metest` tests linear and nonlinear combinations of the marginal effects
reported by [`mecompare`](../mecompare/index.html) -- or of any results posted by
`margins, post`. Rows are referred to by the number in the `#` column of the
`mecompare` table, so a difference between two effects is `metest 2 - 1`, a ratio is
`metest 2 / 1`, and a test that several effects are equal is
`metest 1 = 2 = 3`. To refer to an actual number for a mathematical expression,
use a leading # -- e.g. to divide the 5th marginal effect by 2 use `metest 5 / #2`.

Sums, differences, ratios, products, and functions such as `abs()`, `exp()`,
`ln()`, and `min()` are all allowed, as are equality tests with `=`, including
several at once. Results can be accumulated into one table with `add`.

## Installation

`metest` is part of the `mecompare` package and is installed with it:

```stata
net install mecompare, from("https://tdmize.github.io/data") replace
```

`metest` requires Stata 16 or later.

## Where to start

- [Usage and examples](usage.html) runs every form of the command from the
  help file: single effects, differences, ratios and averages, scaling by a
  literal value, equality tests, accumulated tables, and use after commands other
  than `mecompare`.
- [Tests across three or more models](many-models.html) compares one effect
  across four nested models.
- The [help file](help.html) is on the site.
- The `mecompare` pages use `metest` throughout, e.g. the [effect sizes across
  predictors](../mecompare/examples/within-model.html) example and the
  [interactions pages](../mecompare/interactions/index.html).

## Basic use

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
sysuse nlsw88, clear
drop if missing(union)

quietly logit union i.collgrad i.south i.smsa c.age c.wage, vce(robust)
estimates store m

mecompare i.collgrad i.south i.smsa, models(m)
<</dd_do>>
```

Is the college gap in union membership the same size as the regional gap? And
is the college gap larger than the city/non-city gap?

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
metest 1 - 2
metest 1 - 3
<</dd_do>>
```
